stages.name: Las Condes
stages.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: SNES 2D fighting-game stage master, one standalone wide background. Input images: Image 1 is the exact Las Condes architecture reference photo; preserve its identifiable building proportions and facade. Image 2 is a style/color reference for the existing Abaqus After Hours cartoon arcade art; do not copy its composition. Primary request: Create a polished original 1993-era Super Nintendo fighting-game cartoon background for the Las Condes stage in Santiago, Chile, based on the supplied photo. Scene/backdrop: recognizable corporate glass entrance at address 140, viewed straight-on from the fighter's side, at blue hour with warm office lights visible through the glass. Subject: the actual entrance architecture: two huge tall silver cylindrical columns, broad glass canopy, revolving glass entrance, glass facade, and the exact large white number “140” on the dark entrance wall. A burgundy/red-leaf tree dominates the right side, with the tiled sidewalk and low glass railing at the right. Subtle Andes reflection in the upper glass. Style/medium: colorful hand-placed pixel-art illustration with chunky flat color clusters, strong dark navy contour lines, cel-shaded 16-bit arcade finish, playful cartoon proportions but faithful architectural reference, no photorealism, no painterly blur. Target final framing is 8:7 landscape, 1024x896 master that can reduce cleanly to 256x224 and upscale 4x with nearest-neighbor. Composition/framing: wide 8:7 panorama, side-on fighting-game view. Keep HUD-safe upper band clean and architectural. Leave the lower quarter as an empty flat tiled fighting floor from x=0..255, beginning around native y=168, with a clear feet line around native y=201. Keep fighter head space calm from native y=72 to 130; place the recognizable columns and canopy in the upper/mid background. No foreground people or cars. No text except the exact number “140” on the building. Lighting/mood: elegant Santiago blue hour, warm golden office windows, readable silhouettes, a refined arcade stage mood. Color palette: cobalt and glass blues, warm amber window light, silver columns, cream concrete, burgundy foliage, deep navy outlines; disciplined circa-1993 SNES palette, about 90 colors. Materials/textures: glass reflections, brushed silver, tiled sidewalk, crisp pixel dithering used sparingly. Constraints: architectural fidelity to the attached Las Condes photo is highest priority; the building must read as that photo at native size; two huge tall silver columns must be visible; canopy and revolving entrance must be visible; exact “140” must be clearly legible; empty continuous fight floor lower quarter; no UI, no health bars, no fighters, no logos, no watermark. Avoid: generic temple, palace, futuristic sci-fi tower, extra arches, photorealistic rendering, soft airbrush, noisy tiny detail, blurry edges, commercial game sprites, Street Fighter characters, Capcom logos, extra signage, extra words.
